method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Take a detailed drug allergy history** to guide the antibiotic choice.
claims.source_text: A detailed drug allergy history should be taken to help make appropriate antibiotic choices
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Immediate or severe reaction to either a penicillin or a cephalosporin: avoid drugs from both β-lactam classes.**
claims.source_text: Children with a history of an immediate or severe reaction to either a penicillin or cephalosporin should avoid drugs from both β-lactam classes
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Non-immediate and non-severe reaction: an antibiotic from the alternate β-lactam class can be prescribed.**
claims.source_text: Children with a history of non-immediate and non-severe reactions can be prescribed an antibiotic from an alternate β-lactam class
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Drug allergy testing (drug challenge or skin testing) belongs in controlled settings.**
claims.source_text: Drug allergy testing (drug challenge or skin testing) should take place in controlled settings
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Up to a quarter of children presenting to hospital report an antibiotic allergy. **More than 90% of children with non-immediate β-lactam reactions do not react again when re-challenged** with the same drug.
claims.source_text: Up to a quarter of all children presenting to hospital will report an antibiotic allergy … More than 90% of children with non-immediate β-lactam reactions do not have a reproducible ‘allergic’ reaction when re-challenged with the same drug
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Three quarters of children who identify as penicillin-allergic do so by 3 years of age.
claims.source_text: Three quarters of all children who identify as “allergic” to penicillin will do so by 3 years of age
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Timing:** symptoms under 1 hour after ingestion = **immediate**; over 1 hour = **delayed**. Record the duration of symptoms and time to recovery.
claims.source_text: Timing of reaction Symptoms occur <1 hour after ingestion (= immediate) Occur >1 hour after ingestion (= delayed) Duration of symptoms and time to recovery
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Type of reaction:** rash (non-specific, maculopapular, urticarial) · respiratory symptoms (wheeze, stridor, increased work of breathing) · dizziness or collapse · airway angioedema (mouth, eyes, lips, tongue) · mucous membrane involvement · gastrointestinal symptoms · joint and muscle pain · whether immediate treatment was needed (adrenaline auto-injector, bronchodilator) · previous anaphylaxis.
claims.source_text: Type of reaction Rash (eg non-specific, maculopapular, urticarial) Respiratory symptoms (eg wheeze, stridor or increased work of breathing) Dizziness or collapse Airway angioedema (mouth, eyes, lips, or tongue) Mucous membrane involvement Gastrointestinal symptoms Joint and muscle pain Other Required immediate treatment (eg adrenaline auto injector, bronchodilator) Previous episode of anaphylaxis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also record:** concurrent drugs · concurrent illness (e.g. possible viral infection) · **antibiotics tolerated since, especially after the reported reaction** · other drug and non-drug allergies · atopic disease. No specific examination is required.
claims.source_text: Concurrently administered drugs Concurrent illness (eg possible viral infection) Antibiotics previously tolerated (especially those after the reported reaction) Past history of other drug and non-drug allergies Atopic disease … No specific examination required – be guided by current presentation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Immediate (<1 hour), severe** (airway angioedema, bronchospasm or anaphylaxis): **avoid all drugs from the same β-lactam class and those with potential for cross-reactivity.** **Immediate, non-severe** (e.g. isolated urticaria, pruritus): may consider a non-cross-reactive drug from the alternate β-lactam class.
claims.source_text: Immediate (<1 hour) For severe reactions (airway angioedema, bronchospasm or anaphylaxis): avoid all drugs from the same β-lactam class and those with potential for cross reactivity (see table) For non-severe reactions (eg isolated urticaria, pruritus): may consider non-cross reactive drug from alternate β-lactam class
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Delayed (>1 hour), suspected severe cutaneous adverse reaction (SCAR): avoid all β-lactams.** SCARs include Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, DRESS and acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis. **Cytopenias, acute kidney or drug-induced liver injury:** discuss with the local paediatric team or drug allergy service.
claims.source_text: Delayed (>1 hour) For suspected severe cutaneous adverse reaction (SCAR)*: avoid all β-lactams For cytopenias, acute kidney or drug-induced liver injury: discuss with local paediatric team or drug allergy service … * SCARs include: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS), Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN), drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) and acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Delayed reactions: all non-β-lactam antibiotics, or aztreonam, are safe to prescribe.** Non-severe delayed reactions (e.g. pruritus or isolated exanthem): **a β-lactam from the alternative class is safe.**
claims.source_text: Delayed (>1 hour) For suspected severe cutaneous adverse reaction (SCAR)*: avoid all β-lactams For cytopenias, acute kidney or drug-induced liver injury: discuss with local paediatric team or drug allergy service Safe to prescribe all non β-lactam antibiotics or aztreonam For non-severe reactions (eg pruritus or isolated exanthem), it is safe to prescribe β-lactam from alternative class
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Timing unknown:** treat a severe reaction as immediate-severe, and a non-severe reaction as delayed-non-severe.
claims.source_text: Timing unknown Severe reaction: treat as per immediate, severe reaction Non-severe reaction: treat as per delayed, non-severe reaction
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer for drug allergy assessment and document the allergy** in the medical record pending the outcome.
claims.source_text: Refer for drug allergy assessment and document allergy in the medical record pending outcome
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Unlikely allergy** — known drug side effects (e.g. nausea, headache) or a family history only: **all β-lactams are safe; remove the drug allergy label.**
claims.source_text: Timing known but unlikely allergy: Known drug side effects (eg nausea, headache) family history only Safe to administer all β-lactam drugs Remove drug allergy label
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: After an immediate reaction to a penicillin or cephalosporin, **the highest chance of cross-reactivity is with a β-lactam sharing an R1 side chain.**
claims.source_text: For children with an immediate reaction to a penicillin or cephalosporin, the highest chance of cross reactivity is with a β-lactam that shares an R1-side chain
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspected amoxicillin or ampicillin allergy: avoid cefalexin and cefaclor** — except for non-immediate and non-severe reactions.
claims.source_text: For suspected amoxicillin or ampicillin allergy - avoid cefalexin and cefaclor (except for non-immediate and non-severe reactions - see above)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected ceftriaxone allergy: avoid cefotaxime and cefepime.**
claims.source_text: Suspected ceftriaxone allergy – avoid cefotaxime and cefepime
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Penicillin–carbapenem cross-reactivity (e.g. imipenem, meropenem) is rare — around 1%.**
claims.source_text: Cross reactivity between penicillin and carbapenems (eg imipenem, meropenem) is rare – around 1%
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the local paediatric team:** any child with a clear history of immediate or severe antibiotic allergy; children with non-severe reactions who need urgent or ongoing antibiotics. **Either immediate or non-immediate reactions may be referred to an outpatient allergy clinic** for formal assessment.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Any child with a clear history of immediate or severe antibiotic allergy Children with history of non-severe reactions who require urgent or ongoing antibiotic therapy … Children with either immediate or non-immediate reactions may be referred to an outpatient allergy clinic for formal drug allergy assessment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antibiotic prescribing in children with reported penicillin or cephalosporin allergy' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antibiotic_prescribing_in_children_with_reported_penicillin_or_cephalosporin_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23
